summary: This note is a collection of excerpts from the Wikipedia article on the United States Air Force, covering its fighter aircraft and their missions, its recently streamlined core functions, the civilian and uniformed leadership structure of the Department of the Air Force, the Assure/Dissuade/Deter mission set, the peacetime organization and wartime control of units, command and control, the dangerous support career fields, and Offensive Counterair. The fighter section notes the F-16 and F-4 Phantom II roles and the USAF fighter count as of September 2012. The organizational sections describe how units are chopped to combatant commanders when needed.
one_line: Wikipedia excerpts on the US Air Force covering its fighter fleet, core functions, leadership structure, deterrence mission, command and control, and offensive counterair.
key_facts: The USAF has 2,025 fighters in service as of September 2012.
The F-16 Fighting Falcon is currently used by the USAF Air Demonstration squadron, the Thunderbirds.
Some F-4 Phantom II aircraft are retained as QF-4 aircraft for use as Full Scale Aerial Targets (FSAT) or as part of the USAF Heritage Flight program.
Early model F-16 aircraft converted to QF-16 configuration are replacing QF-4 aircraft in the FSAT role.
The Air Force streamlined six distinctive capabilities and seventeen operational functions into twelve core functions.
The Department of the Air Force is one of three military departments within the Department of Defense.
The Department of the Air Force is managed by the civilian Secretary of the Air Force, under the authority, direction, and control of the Secretary of Defense.
The Under Secretary of the Air Force, four Assistant Secretaries of the Air Force and the General Counsel are appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate.
The senior uniformed leadership in the Air Staff is the Chief of Staff of the Air Force and the Vice Chief of Staff of the Air Force.

Assure/Dissuade/Deter is a mission set derived from the Air Force's readiness to carry out the nuclear strike operations mission and from actions taken to assure allies as part of extended deterrence.

When required to support operational missions, the Secretary of Defense directs the Secretary of the Air Force to execute a Change in Operational Control (CHOP) of units to a Regional Combatant Commander.
AFSPC, AFSOC, PACAF, and USAFE forces are normally employed in-place under their existing CCDR.
AMC forces operating in support roles retain their componency to USTRANSCOM unless chopped to a Regional CCDR.
Command and control is defined in JP 1-02 as the exercise of authority and direction by a properly designated commander over assigned and attached forces.
Offensive Counterair (OCA) is defined in JP 1-02 as offensive operations to destroy, disrupt, or neutralize enemy aircraft, missiles, launch platforms, and their supporting structures and systems.
OCA is described as the preferred method of countering air and missile threats because it typically enjoys the initiative and defeats the enemy closer to its source.
